name: User
rationale: Represents the common authenticated actor type for login and session-scoped actions.
plain_english_summary: A person who can sign in to iTrust.
source_excerpt: ordinary authenticated user

name: User__mid
rationale: MID is the user identifier entered during role-based login and must be represented for credentials.
plain_english_summary: The user's medical ID or login identifier.
source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.
alternatives_considered: Could be modeled only on Patient, but the spec says any user enters their MID.

name: User__name
rationale: Name is needed for patient creation and provider-list search.
plain_english_summary: The user's name.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.
alternatives_considered: Could duplicate name on Patient and Personnel, but User is the shared identity base.

name: User__email
rationale: Email is initially supplied when creating a patient user.
plain_english_summary: The user's email address.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.
alternatives_considered: Could model as Patient-only, but patient is also entered as a new user.

name: HCP
rationale: HCP is a principal role with patient creation and patient-data editing capabilities.
plain_english_summary: A health care provider user.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: LHCP
rationale: LHCP is a specialized HCP role used for provider designations, hospital assignment, and UAP creation.
plain_english_summary: A licensed health care provider.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: LHCP__specialty
rationale: The administrator must specify an LHCP specialty and patients may search by specialty.
plain_english_summary: The licensed provider's medical specialty.
source_excerpt: The administrator must specify the specialty for a new LHCP.
alternatives_considered: Could be an enum entity, but the spec does not provide a closed list of specialties.

name: LHCP__hospitals
rationale: LHCP-to-hospital assignment must support multiple hospitals.
plain_english_summary: The hospitals where this LHCP is assigned.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.
alternatives_considered: Could be modeled as a separate Assignment entity, but the slice only needs the relationship.

name: Administrator
rationale: Administrator is a principal role for creating personnel and configuring inactivity periods.
plain_english_summary: An administrative iTrust user.
source_excerpt: administrator

name: Patient
rationale: Patient is both a principal and a protected subject for records, logs, providers, and demographics.
plain_english_summary: A patient in iTrust.
source_excerpt: patient

name: Patient__demographicInformation
rationale: Demographic information is an important patient resource in the requirements.
plain_english_summary: The patient's demographic details.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patients, personnel, medical records, demographic information, provider designations, access logs, sessions, credentials, and provider lists.
alternatives_considered: Could be a separate DemographicInformation entity, but no independent actions target it in this slice.

name: Patient__providerList
rationale: Patients add providers to their own provider list.
plain_english_summary: The patient's list of providers.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Could use Set<HCP> directly, but provider-list operations are named as a resource.

name: Patient__designatedProviders
rationale: DLHCP is patient-specific and should be represented as a designation relationship rather than a global role only.
plain_english_summary: The LHCPs designated by this patient as designated providers.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.
alternatives_considered: Modeled DLHCP as a separate principal type, but the spec emphasizes designation for that patient.

name: Patient__personalRepresentatives
rationale: Personal-representative access depends on a patient-specific relationship.
plain_english_summary: The users who may act as this patient's personal representatives.
source_excerpt: for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative
alternatives_considered: Could model represented patients on PersonalRepresentative, but record authorization naturally checks the record's patient.

name: PersonalRepresentative
rationale: Personal representative is a principal type allowed to view represented patients' medical records.
plain_english_summary: A user who can act on behalf of a patient.
source_excerpt: personal representative

name: UAP
rationale: UAP is a user role created by LHCPs.
plain_english_summary: A user role called UAP in iTrust.
source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

name: EmergencyResponder
rationale: Emergency responders are personnel users created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: An emergency responder user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: PublicHealthAgent
rationale: Public health agents are personnel users created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A public health agent user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: Hospital
rationale: Hospitals are assignment targets for LHCPs.
plain_english_summary: A hospital that an LHCP can be assigned to.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.

name: ProviderList
rationale: Provider lists are explicitly named resources that patients update.
plain_english_summary: A patient's list of health care providers.
source_excerpt: provider lists

name: ProviderList__patient
rationale: Provider-list changes are patient-owned and need an owner link.
plain_english_summary: The patient who owns this provider list.
source_excerpt: their provider list
alternatives_considered: Could rely on action context only, but ownership is persistent on the list.

name: ProviderList__providers
rationale: The provider list must contain HCP/LHCP providers added by the patient.
plain_english_summary: The providers on the list.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Could maintain separate LHCP and HCP sets, but LHCP is a member of HCP.

name: MedicalRecord
rationale: Medical records are protected resources viewed by patients and personal representatives.
plain_english_summary: A patient's medical record.
source_excerpt: medical records including family history

name: MedicalRecord__patient
rationale: Record access is restricted to own or represented-patient records.
plain_english_summary: The patient this medical record belongs to.
source_excerpt: their own records and for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative

name: MedicalRecord__familyHistory
rationale: Family history is explicitly included in viewable medical records.
plain_english_summary: The family-history portion of the medical record.
source_excerpt: medical records including family history
alternatives_considered: Could be a separate FamilyHistory entity, but the spec treats it as included medical-record information.

name: MedicalRecord__personalHealthInformation
rationale: Personal health information is a named part of records that may be seen.
plain_english_summary: The personal health information in the record.
source_excerpt: patient personal health information
alternatives_considered: Could be a separate entity, but no independent lifecycle is specified.

name: MedicalRecord__immunizations
rationale: Immunizations are a named part of records that may be seen.
plain_english_summary: The immunization information in the record.
source_excerpt: immunizations
alternatives_considered: Could be a Set<Immunization> entity, but no attributes for individual immunizations are specified.

name: MedicalRecord__officeVisitInformation
rationale: Office-visit information is a named part of records that may be seen.
plain_english_summary: The office-visit information in the record.
source_excerpt: office-visit information
alternatives_considered: Could be a separate OfficeVisit entity, but this slice only requires viewing the record section.

name: AccessLog
rationale: Access logs are patient-owned resources viewable over a chosen date range.
plain_english_summary: A log of accesses to a patient's information.
source_excerpt: access logs

name: AccessLog__patient
rationale: Patients view their own access log, so the log needs an owner link.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose access log this is.
source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log.

name: AccessLog__entries
rationale: The access-log result contains structured entry data.
plain_english_summary: The entries shown in an access-log result.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.
cedar_type: Set<Record { accessorName: String, accessorRole: String, accessTimestamp: datetime, transactionType: String }>
alternatives_considered: Could define a reusable type alias, but this shape appears only once.

name: Session
rationale: Sessions represent the authenticated boundary and inactivity termination state for protected actions.
plain_english_summary: A user's active iTrust login session.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: Session__user
rationale: A session belongs to the authenticated user whose actions it authorizes.
plain_english_summary: The user signed in for this session.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: Session__isActive
rationale: Authorization is disabled after logout, close, or inactivity expiry, so active state must be represented.
plain_english_summary: Whether the session is still active.
source_excerpt: after the inactivity limit is exceeded, all authorization is disabled.
alternatives_considered: Could use expiresAt only, but logout and application close also end a session.

name: Session__inactivityPeriodLength
rationale: The administrator can configure the inactivity period length.
plain_english_summary: The configured inactivity timeout for the session.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.
alternatives_considered: Could model a global SystemSettings entity, but the session boundary is the authorization hook requested by the spec.

name: Credentials
rationale: Credentials hold password and security-question data that HCPs must not enter, edit, or view for patients.
plain_english_summary: A user's private login credential information.
source_excerpt: credentials

name: Credentials__user
rationale: Credential secrecy rules refer to a patient's security question and password.
plain_english_summary: The user these credentials belong to.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

name: Credentials__password
rationale: Password is a protected credential field used for login and password changes.
plain_english_summary: The user's password credential.
source_excerpt: password
alternatives_considered: Could omit secret values from schema, but explicit field-level secrecy is required.

name: Credentials__securityQuestion
rationale: Security question is explicitly protected from HCP entry, editing, and viewing.
plain_english_summary: The user's security question credential.
source_excerpt: security question
alternatives_considered: Could group with password in an opaque secret record, but the spec names this field separately.

name: createPatient
rationale: HCPs can create patients and enter them as new users.
plain_english_summary: Create a new patient user.
source_excerpt: An HCP can create a patient and enter the patient as a new user of the system.

session.name: createPatient__context__session
session.rationale: Protected creation requires an active authenticated session.
session.plain_english_summary: The login session for this request.
session.source_excerpt: An HCP can create a patient and enter the patient as a new user of the system.

name: editPatientData
rationale: HCPs can edit patient data but policies must exclude non-editable MID and credentials.
plain_english_summary: Edit patient information.
source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format, but the patient's MID must not be editable.

session.name: editPatientData__context__session
session.rationale: Protected editing requires an active authenticated session.
session.plain_english_summary: The login session for this request.
session.source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format, but the patient's MID must not be editable.

session.name: createPublicHealthAgent__context__session
session.rationale: Protected creation requires an active authenticated session.
session.plain_english_summary: The login session for this request.
session.source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: assignLHCPToHospital
rationale: Administrators assign LHCPs to one or more hospitals.
plain_english_summary: Assign an LHCP to hospitals.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.

session.name: assignLHCPToHospital__context__session

session.plain_english_summary: The login session for this request.
session.source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.

hospitals.rationale: The administrator chooses the hospitals for the LHCP.

source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

session.name: createUAP__context__session

name: login
rationale: Users enter MID and password to gain role-based entry.
plain_english_summary: Sign in to iTrust.
source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

credentials.name: login__context__credentials
credentials.rationale: Login depends on the user's MID and password credentials.
credentials.source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

name: requestPasswordChange
rationale: Any user can request a password change.
plain_english_summary: Ask to change your password.
source_excerpt: Any user can request a password change.

session.name: requestPasswordChange__context__session
session.rationale: Password-change requests are made by an authenticated user.
session.plain_english_summary: The login session for this request.
session.source_excerpt: Any user can request a password change.

name: logout
rationale: Logging out ends an authenticated session.
plain_english_summary: End the current iTrust session by logging out.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: closeApplication
rationale: Closing the application ends an authenticated session.
plain_english_summary: End the current iTrust session by closing the application.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: setInactivityPeriodLength
rationale: Administrators can configure the inactivity timeout.

source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

session.name: setInactivityPeriodLength__context__session
session.rationale: Protected configuration requires an active administrator session.
session.source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: viewProviderHistory

session.name: viewProviderHistory__context__session

session.plain_english_summary: The login session for this request.
session.source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.

session.plain_english_summary: The login session for this request.

session.name: viewAccessLog__context__session
session.rationale: Protected viewing requires an active authenticated session.
session.plain_english_summary: The login session for this request.
session.source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log. The patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period.

beginDate.name: viewAccessLog__context__beginDate
beginDate.rationale: The patient chooses the beginning date for the access-log period.
beginDate.plain_english_summary: The start of the log period.

endDate.name: viewAccessLog__context__endDate
endDate.rationale: The patient chooses the end date for the access-log period.

session.name: viewMedicalRecord__context__session
session.rationale: Protected viewing requires an active authenticated session.
session.plain_english_summary: The login session for this request.
session.source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history.
